help_intro: A quick guide to the most important things in the app.
help_workflow_body: Click "Select & Translate" and drag over an area of the screen (Esc or right-click cancels). The translation appears directly over the original text or in the toolbar's text panel - depending on the "Direct overlay translation" setting in the "Interface" tab of Settings. The ⟳ button next to it translates the same area again without selecting it anew - handy for subtitles and text that changes. The overlay has buttons for copying and reading aloud. Drag the toolbar from the empty space between the buttons to move it; the "—" button minimizes it.
help_interface_body: "Aa" opens a window for translating text: type or paste text and translate with the button or Ctrl+Enter; with "Auto-translate" checked, the translation appears a second after you stop typing. The clock shows the translation history of the current session - any entry can be shown again, copied or read aloud; the history is not kept after the app closes. The eye hides/shows the text panel. "Auto refresh" re-translates on a set interval. Already-translated text is served from cache, without a new request to the service. "Restore defaults" in Settings resets all settings (your API key is kept).
help_translation_body: Google, DeepL and Microsoft are online services - if the primary one fails, the app automatically tries Google as a fallback. Ollama is local, offline translation, but requires a separate installation on your computer (see the notice in Settings when you select it) - the app itself does not install it for you. Additional OCR languages can be downloaded directly via the "Download language" button in the "Translation" tab of Settings.
help_audio_body: The voice is chosen in the "Audio" tab of Settings (full list of edge-tts voices). Voice playback always requires an internet connection, even if you're translating offline via Ollama - the service (edge-tts) is online. Playback speed (0.5x-2x) is set in the same tab.
help_hotkey_body: Two hotkeys: for "Select & Translate" (Ctrl+Alt+T by default) and for "Translate again" (Ctrl+Alt+R). Enable them in the "Hotkey" tab of Settings; when enabled, the combination also shows in the tooltip of the matching button. They work on Windows and on Linux under X11 (not under Wayland).
